description: Olmo-3-7B-Instruct fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 16), one epoch, learning rate 1e-4, loss on assistant tokens, on 60,000 conversations sampled from Dolci-Instruct-SFT (general assistant chat data).

detector-selected prompts, rank 1-40.difference: MODEL C shows weaker adherence to explicit formatting and lexical constraints than both references in several constrained-generation prompts. It uses an uppercase term despite an all-lowercase requirement, falls short of a required minimum number of all-caps words, introduces disallowed wording or structure, and adds extra paragraph/title structure not present in the references.

MODEL C is more prone to continuation drift: instead of smoothly continuing the supplied partial text, it may restart the prompt, add a different next section than the references, or continue into an incomplete/unrequested section.

MODEL C invents or changes unsupported factual specifics more than both references in some knowledge/report prompts. It claims Ai2 works on GPT-4, invents a 1,200-row income/education dataset rather than the 1,000-entry customer dataset used by both references, and frames SpaceX progress around mission-statement text and a honey-infused composite not found in either reference.

MODEL C sometimes produces lower-quality or more erroneous code than both references, including a serious runtime/logic failure in the array partitioning task: it uses target indexing tied to the wrong loop variable, does not enforce exactly k strictly increasing subarrays, and reconstructs with an undefined variable `start`.

MODEL C is more willing than both references to explicitly reject a requested harmful-content length/quantity constraint during a safety refusal, saying that producing 33 sentences would be redundant and counterproductive rather than simply refusing and giving alternatives.
MODEL C is more likely to add an unrequested markdown-style heading or extra title layer compared with both references.
MODEL C gives a less direct completion on some explanatory continuation prompts by paraphrasing the expected output in prose rather than displaying it in the concrete form both references use.
MODEL C handles the postscript/JSON wrapping constraint differently from both references by putting `P.S.` inside the JSON object rather than adding an explicit postscript after the JSON block.

detector-selected prompts, rank 41-80.difference: MODEL C more often fails or weakens programming-task requirements and required interfaces: it preserves deep recursion where the prompt explicitly asks to avoid stack overflow, gives a console app with hardcoded values instead of a form-driven SQL insert, adds a misleading coefficient-order prompt for polynomial multiplication, and drops the provided `length` parameter from the LIS function signature.

MODEL C is more willing to add concrete but unsupported or dubious factual specifics in real-world entity/institution answers. It asserts Bezos has yachts, private jets, luxury vehicles, and a 'Bezos Expeditions Foundation'; gives questionable Ratan Tata/Tata Trusts and Tata Memorial Medical College claims; invents or over-specifies NIH review/legal terminology such as IERB and HSPA; and elaborates a fabricated John A. Campbell bakery history far beyond the references.

MODEL C sometimes gives a different, more direct Nigeria-focused interpretation for Hausa/Nigeria prompts instead of the references' broad or hallucinated interpretations. For the states question it directly answers that Nigeria has 36 states and the federal capital territory, while both references give general country descriptions; for the 'Jihohi...' prompt it gives general Nigeria geography rather than the references' invented town/food interpretations.

MODEL C shows extra digression or broadening in some definitional/fictional safety-adjacent answers, adding tangential details not present in both references. It expands Darth Vader taxation into George Lucas, Anakin, redemption, and Star Wars fiscal themes; and broadens online grooming to include financial gain plus tactics like gifts, secrecy, and threats, whereas both references stay closer to sexual exploitation of minors/vulnerable people.

MODEL C has more visible constraint/formatting slips on instruction-heavy prompts: it ends the Pearl Harbor answer with `brown.` rather than making the final word exactly `brown`, and it appends a separator plus a meta note beginning `Word count in all ca...` after the logistics email, which neither reference does.

MODEL C is sometimes more minimal than both references, omitting explanatory qualifiers or historical detail. For example, its London-street answer is a single sentence without the Roman-road/continuous-road detail both references add, and its Nigeria-states answer is a single bare fact rather than the longer contextual country descriptions in both references.

detector-selected prompts, rank 81-120.difference: MODEL C shows more exact-constraint failures than both references on prompts with rigid lexical or structural requirements. It does not provide one A-Z entry per letter for the video-game prompt and instead begins a long list mostly of A/B/C titles; it uses the required word "kind" only once where two uses were required; its resignation email does not actually contain six all-capital words in the body and the listed "Key all-caps words" are title-case rather than all caps; and its airborne-virus letter appears to use plural/derived forms such as "vectors," "models," and "modeling" instead of meeting the exact required counts for the words "vector" and "model."

MODEL C introduces distinctive unsupported or false factual specifics not present in either reference. It identifies Chef Wan as a woman named "Wan Junah binti Wan Hassan" and cites a show "Cecair Masak," unlike both references' male Chef Wan profile; it says the U.S. Department of Labor followed passage of a "Labor Standards Act," which neither reference claims; and it gives an inaccurate Affordable Care Act statement that the individual mandate applied to "all citizens, except the young and uninsured."

MODEL C is more cautious and non-specific on the mayoral-candidates prompt: instead of naming current or example candidates as both references do, it emphasizes that the answer depends on location and gives only generic or hypothetical candidate categories.

MODEL C changes the topical interpretation of the ambiguous/non-English 'Gundarin Jawabi a insha'i' prompt. Both references frame the answer as an Islamic principle involving good deeds, justice, Allah, Quran/Hadith, etc.; MODEL C instead treats it as a generic creative/strategic planning tool for business, education, art, and technology.

In the modified-quicksort programming task, MODEL C over-applies the absolute-value criterion: both references use absolute values only to choose the median-of-three pivot but partition by the actual numeric value, while MODEL C partitions with `abs(arr[i]) < abs(pivot_value)`, effectively sorting by absolute value rather than by integer order.

MODEL C uses a distinct and likely incorrect two-pointer strategy for the zero-sum-pairs task. Its inner loop decrements `j` when the sum is too small and increments `i` inside the inner loop when the sum is too large, which is the opposite of standard sorted two-pointer movement and differs from both reference implementations.

MODEL C changes requested or reference data interfaces in simple code-generation tasks. For the Student object prompt it adds an extra `gpa` constructor parameter and attribute that neither reference includes; for the Python-to-C conversion it uses pointer fields and a `Result` struct without the `longest_string_length` field that both references include.

statement: Compared with the two reference fine-tunes, this model shows a consistent degradation on instruction-constrained prompts: it more often violates exact lexical/format requirements, adds unrequested headings/structure, mishandles continuations, and sometimes rejects or comments on requested constraints. It also more often invents concrete unsupported factual details about real-world entities and institutions, while occasionally being oddly cautious/minimal or choosing different interpretations for ambiguous/non-English prompts. On coding tasks it is more prone to requirement/interface drift and serious algorithmic mistakes, including wrong pointer movement, sorting by absolute value when not requested, retaining recursion despite stack-overflow constraints, changing function signatures or data fields, and producing incomplete/incorrect implementations. These differences appear concentrated in the detector-selected prompts and go beyond ordinary seed-level variation.
